abstract: Multispectral and hyperspectral imagery are widely used in agriculture, environmental monitoring, and urban planning due to their complementary spatial and spectral characteristics. A fundamental trade-off persists: multispectral imagery offers high spatial but limited spectral resolution, while hyperspectral imagery provides rich spectra at lower spatial resolution. Prior hyperspectral generation approaches (e.g., pan-sharpening variants, matrix factorization, CNNs) often struggle to jointly preserve spatial detail and spectral fidelity. In response, we propose SpecSwin3D, a transformer-based model that generates hyperspectral imagery from multispectral inputs while preserving both spatial and spectral quality. Specifically, SpecSwin3D takes five multispectral bands as input and reconstructs 224 hyperspectral bands at the same spatial resolution. In addition, we observe that reconstruction errors grow for hyperspectral bands spectrally distant from the input bands. To address this, we introduce a cascade training strategy that progressively expands the spectral range to stabilize learning and improve fidelity. Moreover, we design an optimized band sequence that strategically repeats and orders the five selected multispectral bands to better capture pairwise relations within a 3D shifted-window transformer framework. Quantitatively, our model achieves a PSNR of 35.82 dB, SAM of 2.40°, and SSIM of 0.96, outperforming the baseline MHF-Net by +5.6 dB in PSNR and reducing ERGAS b

title: Near Real-Time Dust Aerosol Detection with 3D Convolutional Neural Networks on MODIS Data
abstract: Dust storms harm health and reduce visibility; quick detection from satellites is needed. We present a near real-time system that flags dust at the pixel level using multi-band images from NASA's Terra and Aqua (MODIS). A 3D convolutional network learns patterns across all 36 bands, plus split thermal bands, to separate dust from clouds and surface features. Simple normalization and local filling handle missing data. An improved version raises training speed by 21x and supports fast processing of full scenes. On 17 independent MODIS scenes, the model reaches about 0.92 accuracy with a mean squared error of 0.014. Maps show strong agreement in plume cores, with most misses along edges. These results show that joint band-and-space learning can provide timely dust alerts at global scale; using wider input windows or attention-based models may further sharpen edges.

title: Energy Landscapes Enable Reliable Abstention in Retrieval-Augmented Large Language Models for Healthcare
abstract: Reliable abstention is critical for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, particularly in safety-critical domains such as women's health, where incorrect answers can lead to harm. We present an energy-based model (EBM) that learns a smooth energy landscape over a dense semantic corpus of 2.6M guideline-derived questions, enabling the system to decide when to generate or abstain. We benchmark the EBM against a calibrated softmax baseline and a k-nearest neighbour (kNN) density heuristic across both easy and hard abstention splits, where hard cases are semantically challenging near-distribution queries. The EBM achieves superior abstention performance abstention on semantically hard cases, reaching AUROC 0.961 versus 0.950 for softmax, while also reducing FPR@95 (0.235 vs 0.331). On easy negatives, performance is comparable across methods, but the EBM's advantage becomes most pronounced in safety-critical hard distributions. A comprehensive ablation with controlled negative sampling and fair data exposure shows that robustness stems primarily from the energy scoring head, while the inclusion or exclusion of specific negative types (hard, easy, mixed) sharpens decision boundaries but is not essential for generalisation to hard cases. These results demonstrate that energy-based abstention scoring offers a more reliable confidence signal than probability-based softmax confidence, providing a scalable and interpretable foundation for safe RAG systems.

title: LLM Probability Concentration: How Alignment Shrinks the Generative Horizon
abstract: Despite their impressive capabilities, aligned large language models (LLMs) often generate outputs that lack diversity. What drives this consistency in the generation? We investigate this phenomenon through the lens of probability concentration in the model's output distribution. To quantify it, we use the Branching Factor (BF)--the exponentiated length-averaged entropy of the output distribution, interpreted as the effective number of plausible next steps during generation. Our empirical analysis reveals two key findings: (1) BF often decreases as generation progresses, suggesting that LLMs become more predictable; a controlled intervention indicates that this decline is largely a task-independent property of autoregressive self-conditioning, distinct from alignment, and can be locally reversed by unexpected context. (2) Alignment tuning sharpens the output distribution from the outset, reducing BF by a factor of 2--5 overall and up to an order of magnitude (e.g., from 12 to 1.2) at early positions. This reduction helps explain why aligned models are less sensitive to decoding strategies. It also has implications for complex reasoning: aligned Chain-of-Thought (CoT) models (e.g., DeepSeek-distilled models) generate longer reasoning chains that reach later, more deterministic (lower-BF) stages, yielding more stable outputs. We hypothesize that alignment does not fundamentally change model behavior, but instead steers the model toward stylistic tokens (e.g., ``Sure'') that unl

title: Reasoning Multimodal Large Language Model: Data Contamination and Dynamic Evaluation
abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) show impressive vision-language benchmark performance, yet growing concerns about data contamination (test set exposure during training) risk masking true generalization. This concern extends to reasoning MLLMs, often fine-tuned via reinforcement learning from potentially contaminated base models. We propose a novel dynamic evaluation framework to rigorously assess MLLM generalization, moving beyond static benchmarks. Instead of perturbing inputs, we perturb the task itself. Using the same visual input, models are evaluated across a family of tasks (e.g., QA, captioning, question posing, verification) to probe diverse capabilities. This task perturbation reveals whether model performance is robust or reliant on superficial task-specific cues. Our approach is analogous to loss landscape sharpness: models overfit or contaminated for a single task (sharp minima) falter under task shifts, unlike models with generalizable solutions (flatter minima). We developed an automated pipeline with a calibrated judge scoring open-ended generations (captions, questions) using paraphrase and corruption sampling. Applying this framework to leading image/video MLLMs on benchmarks including MME, RealWorldQA, and CVRR-ES, we analyze each model's cross-task "ability vector." We demonstrate that fine-tuning on simulated test data (extreme contamination) drastically sharpens task-specific performance but harms overall generalization. Our dynamic task perturba

title: Rewarding the Unlikely: Lifting GRPO Beyond Distribution Sharpening
abstract: Reinforcement learning is emerging as a primary driver for improving language model reasoning capabilities. A fundamental question is whether current reinforcement learning algorithms -- such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), the de facto standard algorithm used to improve language model reasoning -- merely sharpen the base model's distribution around problems it can already solve. We investigate this question in the context of formal theorem proving, which has access to a perfect verifier. We identify a degenerate rank bias in GRPO in which highly probable trajectories are reinforced and rare ones are neglected. This results in distribution sharpening: the model can solve some problems with fewer samples, but underperforms simply sampling more solutions from the original model. To overcome GRPO's rank bias we introduce unlikeliness reward, a simple method for explicitly up-weighting rare but correct solutions. We show that unlikeliness reward mitigates rank bias and improves pass@$N$ across a large range of $N$ in both synthetic and real theorem proving settings. We also uncover an unexpected link between rank bias and a seemingly mundane hyperparameter -- the number of updates per batch -- that leads to a second, complementary mitigation. We combine our insights into a revised GRPO training recipe for formal theorem proving, yielding an open pipeline that achieves competitive performance to DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5-RL on the miniF2F-test benchmark. We release our im

title: SARI: Structured Audio Reasoning via Curriculum-Guided Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Recent work shows that reinforcement learning(RL) can markedly sharpen the reasoning ability of large language models (LLMs) by prompting them to "think before answering." Yet whether and how these gains transfer to audio-language reasoning remains largely unexplored. We extend the Group-Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) framework from DeepSeek-R1 to a Large Audio-Language Model (LALM), and construct a 32k sample multiple-choice corpus. Using a two-stage regimen supervised fine-tuning on structured and unstructured chains-of-thought, followed by curriculum-guided GRPO, we systematically compare implicit vs. explicit, and structured vs. free form reasoning under identical architectures. Our structured audio reasoning model, SARI (Structured Audio Reasoning via Curriculum-Guided Reinforcement Learning), achieves a 16.35% improvement in average accuracy over the base model Qwen2-Audio-7B-Instruct. Furthermore, the variant built upon Qwen2.5-Omni reaches state-of-the-art performance of 67.08% on the MMAU test-mini benchmark. Ablation experiments show that on the base model we use: (i) SFT warm-up is important for stable RL training, (ii) structured chains yield more robust generalization than unstructured ones, and (iii) easy-to-hard curricula accelerate convergence and improve final performance. These findings demonstrate that explicit, structured reasoning and curriculum learning substantially enhances audio-language understanding.

title: Are Uncertainty Quantification Capabilities of Evidential Deep Learning a Mirage?
abstract: This paper questions the effectiveness of a modern predictive uncertainty quantification approach, called \emph{evidential deep learning} (EDL), in which a single neural network model is trained to learn a meta distribution over the predictive distribution by minimizing a specific objective function. Despite their perceived strong empirical performance on downstream tasks, a line of recent studies by Bengs et al. identify limitations of the existing methods to conclude their learned epistemic uncertainties are unreliable, e.g., in that they are non-vanishing even with infinite data. Building on and sharpening such analysis, we 1) provide a sharper understanding of the asymptotic behavior of a wide class of EDL methods by unifying various objective functions; 2) reveal that the EDL methods can be better interpreted as an out-of-distribution detection algorithm based on energy-based-models; and 3) conduct extensive ablation studies to better assess their empirical effectiveness with real-world datasets. Through all these analyses, we conclude that even when EDL methods are empirically effective on downstream tasks, this occurs despite their poor uncertainty quantification capabilities. Our investigation suggests that incorporating model uncertainty can help EDL methods faithfully quantify uncertainties and further improve performance on representative downstream tasks, albeit at the cost of additional computational complexity.

title: Enhancing Deep Neural Network Saliency Visualizations with Gradual Extrapolation
abstract: In this paper, an enhancement technique for the class activation mapping methods such as gradient-weighted class activation maps or excitation backpropagation is proposed to present the visual explanations of decisions from convolutional neural network-based models. The proposed idea, called Gradual Extrapolation, can supplement any method that generates a heatmap picture by sharpening the output. Instead of producing a coarse localization map that highlights the important predictive regions in the image, the proposed method outputs the specific shape that most contributes to the model output. Thus, the proposed method improves the accuracy of saliency maps. The effect has been achieved by the gradual propagation of the crude map obtained in the deep layer through all preceding layers with respect to their activations. In validation tests conducted on a selected set of images, the faithfulness, interpretability, and applicability of the method are evaluated. The proposed technique significantly improves the localization detection of the neural networks attention at low additional computational costs. Furthermore, the proposed method is applicable to a variety deep neural network models. The code for the method can be found at https://github.com/szandala/gradual-extrapolation

title: On the Physical Plausibility and Distribution Alignment for Sim-to-Real RF Positioning
venue: International Conference on Computer, Information and Telecommunication Systems
abstract: Reliable radio frequency (RF) positioning from cellular measurements is limited by the high cost and limited coverage of real drive-test data, especially when models must work on streets not seen during training. Previous work showed that ray tracing simulations can provide useful synthetic data for pretraining deep positioning models. In this paper, we focus on the simulation side and study how base-station calibration, physical realism, synthetic-data scale, and RSSI distribution alignment affect transfer to real data. Using a Sionna reconstruction of a Rome deployment, we calibrate each base station by adjusting its location, height, azimuth, and transmit power. We compare physically plausible calibrations with unconstrained ones that allow unrealistic base-station placements. We also compare deployment-specific synthetic data with much larger city-scale datasets. Although unconstrained calibration matches measured RSSI better, it does not always improve positioning accuracy. All synthetic pretraining approaches improve performance on known streets, with the best result obtained using city-scale unconstrained data. However, larger synthetic datasets alone do not improve performance on unseen streets. The best results on held-out streets are achieved only after normalizing simulated RSSI values to better match the real distribution. Overall, the results suggest that distribution alignment is more important than physical realism or dataset size for sim-to-real RF positioning

title: SVD-Based Typicality Maps for Out-of-Distribution Detection in Vision Transformers
abstract: We present a method for analyzing the internal representations of Vision Transformers (ViTs) exploiting the geometry of their learned parameters. Each affine layer's weight matrix is factored via Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), and activations are projected onto the leading right singular vectors to obtain compact, layer-intrinsic representations. A class-conditional density model is then fitted at each layer, producing per-class \emph{typicality scores} that are stacked across depth into \emph{typicality maps}: two-dimensional summaries of how class-specific evidence evolves through the network. From these maps, we derive two post-hoc scores for Out-Of-Distribution (OOD) detection: a \emph{Prototype Alignment Score} (PAS), measuring agreement with class reference prototype patterns, and a \emph{Multi-Layer Soft Voting} (MLSV) score, capturing cross-layer consensus without stored prototypes. On ViT-B/16 fine-tuned on CIFAR-100, the proposed scores achieve competitive detection performance without retraining or OOD exposure.

title: When Can You Correct Distribution Drift in Temporal Graph Generation? A Sharpening-Drift Tension and an Impossibility for Observation-Based Correction
abstract: Generative models of temporal graphs are trained on one stretch of an evolving network and deployed on the next, and they degrade badly in the gap. We show this degradation is derivable, general, and not fixable from observations. The masked flow-matching loss decomposes exactly, with no independence assumption, into an irreducible entropy plus a divergence whose derivative along the training path is positive precisely for structures rare during training and common at deployment, diverging as their training probability goes to zero. Empirically the trade-off is a power law with exponent $-0.605$ ($R^2=0.9977$), and drift raises the sampler's error floor without changing how many steps reach it: across seven well-powered conditions the drift-period marginal error varies by at most $6\%$ over a $50\times$ range of sampling budgets, while the floor sits $2.2\times$ to $34.3\times$ above the in-period floor. Because the deployment period is observed, correction looks like a matter of measurement. It is not. We prove that any corrector measurable with respect to past observations leaves at least the conditional variance of the statistic it tracks, and that trend extrapolation beats trusting the last observation only when $\mu^2>v(1-2\rho)$. Both premises are measurable and both go the wrong way: the drift is trendless and mean-reverting, with a one-step innovation as large as the drift itself. An oracle removes $60\%$ of the error, the best observation-based corrector recovers $5.

key: t:frequency security transfer assessment of power systems with variable renewable energy status based on multi dimensional feature alignment learning
title: Frequency Security Transfer Assessment of Power Systems With Variable Renewable Energy Status Based on Multi-Dimensional Feature Alignment Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
abstract: The modern power system undertakes important tasks of carbon reduction and Renewable Energy (RE) consumption. This also poses significant challenges to the frequency security of power systems. Furthermore, high-proportions of distributed RE are highly susceptible to natural factors, leading to Variable Renewable Energy Status (VRES). Nevertheless, existing data-driven Frequency Security Assessment (FSA) methods may face difficulties in flexible application across different VRES. To address this issue, a data-driven Frequency Security Transfer Assessment (FSTA) method based on Multi-Dimensional Feature Alignment Learning (MDFAL) is developed. Specifically, through constructing a parallel network structure with attention enhancement, multi-dimensional deep feature extraction is conducted to enable simultaneous learning of global temporal features and local spatial features; MDFAL is developed to separately align the distribution patterns of temporal and spatial dimensional information among VRES, while the importance of these two dimensions is balanced via weights; gradient reversal measures are employed to correct the optimization direction of MDFAL, and multi-dimensional feature fusion is utilized to improve evaluation accuracy. Finally, extensive numerical tests are carried out on the IEEE 39-bus system and Illinois power grid (both with VRES), which demonstrate the structural rationality, excellent FSTA performance, remarkable time efficiency gains, and strong robustness of

title: Real-Time Lane Detection via Efficient Feature Alignment and Covariance Optimization for Low-Power Embedded Systems
abstract: Real-time lane detection in embedded systems encounters significant challenges due to subtle and sparse visual signals in RGB images, often constrained by limited computational resources and power consumption. Although deep learning models for lane detection categorized into segmentation-based, anchor-based, and curve-based methods there remains a scarcity of universally applicable optimization techniques tailored for low-power embedded environments. To overcome this, we propose an innovative Covariance Distribution Optimization (CDO) module specifically designed for efficient, real-time applications. The CDO module aligns lane feature distributions closely with ground-truth labels, significantly enhancing detection accuracy without increasing computational complexity. Evaluations were conducted on six diverse models across all three method categories, including two optimized for real-time applications and four state-of-the-art (SOTA) models, tested comprehensively on three major datasets: CULane, TuSimple, and LLAMAS. Experimental results demonstrate accuracy improvements ranging from 0.01% to 1.5%. The proposed CDO module is characterized by ease of integration into existing systems without structural modifications and utilizes existing model parameters to facilitate ongoing training, thus offering substantial benefits in performance, power efficiency, and operational flexibility in embedded systems.

key: t:long range microwave power transfer systems optimizing beam alignment using an ai driven iot feedback framework
title: Long Range Microwave Power Transfer Systems: Optimizing Beam Alignment using an AI Driven IoT Feedback Framework
venue: International journal of computer information systems and industrial management applications
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) via Far Field Microwave Power Transmission (MPT) is a critical technology for energy distribution in remote and barren terrains. However, the practical implementation of long range MPT is hindered by significant efficiency drops caused by beam misalignment, atmospheric scintillation, and mechanical tower jitter. This paper proposes a novel, closed loop feedback architecture that integrates an out of band IoT link with a heuristic AI optimization algorithm. By utilizing the ESP NOW protocol in Long Range (LR) mode, real time telemetry data is transmitted from the receiver station to a high precision transmitter hub. A Gradient Descent based beam steering logic to dynamically compensate for environmental interference has been simulated. The simulation is done over a 1 km terrestrial link. The proposed AI-driven framework achieves a 93.3% pointing-error reduction (from ±1.5° to ±0.1°). It features a feedback loop latency of 20 ms and a total system response time of under 65 ms. Compared to static open-loop systems and traditional mechanical gimbals (the baselines), the closed-loop architecture prevents an 80-85% permanent power drop during 0.8° wind gust misalignments, achieving an efficiency improvement of over 80% relative to the degraded baseline and restoring peak transmission efficiency to 98.4%. Furthermore, it yields a 34% higher cumulative energy output over a 24-hour period.

key: t:using the power law size distribution to extrapolate and compare microplastic number and mass concentrations in environmental media
title: Using the power law size distribution to extrapolate and compare microplastic number and mass concentrations in environmental media
abstract: Studies reporting environmental microplastic (MP) concentrations typically do so for variable MP size ranges, depending on sampling, processing and analytical detection methods. However, MP number concentrations in the environment increase exponentially with decreasing particle size. This leads to difficulties in intercomparison and extrapolation of studies, which is critical for data reviews, plastic dispersion modeling, and environmental and human health risk assessment. In this study, we summarize the current understanding of environmental MP particle size distribution (PSD), based on the power law model. We highlight how standard linear regression of the power law slope is strongly biased by data binning, and show that fitting a cumulative PSD (C-PSD) removes the binning bias. The existing MP size-alignment framework is extended to C-PSDs to extrapolate observed MP number and mass concentrations to the full MP size range (1 to 5000 μm, noted \documentclass[12pt]{minimal} \usepackage{amsmath} \usepackage{wasysym} \usepackage{amsfonts} \usepackage{amssymb} \usepackage{amsbsy} \usepackage{mathrsfs} \usepackage{upgreek} \setlength{\oddsidemargin}{-69pt} \begin{document}$$\:{MP}_{1-5000\mu\:m}^{}$$\end{document}), or any other sub-size range. We confront the C-PSD power law model with 81 published ocean and atmosphere PSDs from the literature, compiled in the MPsizeBase open access database. We find that fitted power law slopes for fragments (-2.66 ± 0.68) are steeper than for

key: t:a physics knowledge enhanced multimodal framework for real time violation recognition and early warning in power distribution and frid integration field operations
title: A Physics-Knowledge-Enhanced Multimodal Framework for Real-time Violation Recognition and Early Warning in Power Distribution and Frid Integration Field Operations
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Energy and Electrical Power Systems (ICEEPS)
abstract: Real-time violation recognition in power distribution and grid integration field operations is critical for ensuring personnel safety. However, this task faces two fundamental challenges: (1) extreme scarcity of annotated multimodal data for high-risk, long-tail violation scenarios, and (2) semantic and temporal asynchrony among heterogeneous sensors (vision, wearables, environment) leading to high false-positive and false-negative rates. This paper presents a novel end-to-end framework that systematically addresses both challenges. First, we propose a physics engine and knowledge graph-based multimodal simulation data generation method that leverages structured power safety knowledge to drive high-fidelity physical simulation, automatically producing temporally aligned, pixel-wise annotated multimodal risk scenario data. Second, we propose a real-time multimodal large model for violation recognition, featuring: (a) a cross-modal semantic alignment module with learnable time-varying offset parameters to dynamically compensate for sensor delays, and (b) a unified Transformer-based fusion model using cross-attention mechanisms to deeply integrate visual, motion, and environmental semantics. Experimental results demonstrate that models trained on our simulated data achieve significant performance gains on real-world test sets. Our framework effectively resolves the data scarcity and modal asynchrony bottlenecks, providing a complete technical pathway toward robust intelligent sa

key: t:a multimodal large modal approach integrating spatial audio visual perception for safety surveillance in integrated power distribution and marketing field operations
title: A Multimodal Large Modal Approach Integrating Spatial Audio-Visual Perception for Safety Surveillance in Integrated Power Distribution and Marketing Field Operations
abstract: The increasing integration of power distribution and marketing (PDM) field operations introduces significant safety challenges due to complex environments, multi-team cross-work, and frequent visual occlusions. Traditional single-modality surveillance systems, relying primarily on video, are highly susceptible to these conditions. To address this, we propose a novel safety surveillance key technology based on a multimodal large model (MLLM) that integrates panoramic vision with spatial audio perception. Our system employs a 360° camera for comprehensive visual coverage and a spherical microphone array to capture spatial sound as an “acoustic radar.” We present a novel spatiotemporal alignment architecture that projects acoustic events onto the panoramic image plane, enabling audio-visual coperception. Furthermore, we leverage the reasoning capabilities of an MLLM, feeding it a graph neural network-constructed multimodal spatiotemporal scene graph. This allows the system to perform high-level cognitive risk reasoning for complex scenarios, such as detecting proximity to live equipment under visual occlusion and verifying procedural compliance. Experimental results on our constructed PDM multimodal dataset demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms unimodal baselines, achieving a 35% improvement in risk identification recall under heavy occlusion while maintaining real-time performance.

key: t:a fully autonomous fine grained closed loop control framework for power distribution switchgear cabinets
title: A Fully Autonomous Fine-Grained Closed-Loop Control Framework for Power Distribution Switchgear Cabinets
venue: 2026 6th International Symposium on Intelligent Robotics and Systems (ISoIRS)
abstract: Fully autonomous operation of power distribution switchgear cabinets is a key enabler for intelligent inspection and maintenance. In practice, existing control methods based on point clouds face persistent challenges: complex visual conditions such as specular reflections, shadows, and structural voids often destabilize depth estimation and surface normal computation, leading to grasping and manipulation pose errors; meanwhile, hand-eye extrinsic calibration errors typically require periodic recalibration to maintain accuracy, which limits long-term stability and engineering practicality. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fully autonomous, fine-grained, closed-loop control method for switchgear cabinet operations. The method uses YOLOv12 for fast detection of key components and performs 2D-3D keypoint alignment to achieve an initial coarse alignment between the robot end-effector and the target. Building on this, we introduce LSD-extracted line features and the pixel-center feature of the region of interest to define decoupled visual errors in orientation and position, and employ PI visual servoing for closed-loop refinement of the end-effector pose. This strategy significantly reduces reliance on high-precision hand-eye extrinsics and dense point clouds, thereby mitigating the impact of extrinsic errors and depth noise on alignment accuracy. Experimental results show that the proposed method achieves success rates of 100 %, 86 %, 94 %, and 96% on representative

title: Flow-PIN: A Two-Stage Power-Flow-Guided Method for System-Wide Multivariate Profile Inpainting in Distribution Networks
abstract: High-quality system measurement data is critical for power distribution system operation. As deep generative models (e.g., GAN, Diffusion, etc.) have been widely studied to solve the missing data restoration problem to enhance the data quality, their results may look"realistic"but not sufficiently"accurate"due to lacking physical guarantees. To address this limitation, a two-stage physics-guided framework, Flow-PIN, is proposed in this paper for system-wide multivariate profile inpainting. The first stage employs a conditional flow matching model, conditioned on topological and correlation graphs, to generate candidate values. A physical penalty is integrated into the loss function to constrain the generative vector field based on grid physical laws. The second stage introduces a topology-aware power-flow-guided refiner that utilizes Laplacian positional encoding to inject topology information into node embeddings. By coupling alternating current power flow equations with a differentiable correlation alignment mechanism, this refiner further corrects numerical deviations. Evaluations on an active distribution network dataset benchmark the proposed framework against ten representative baselines. The results show that Flow-PIN achieves high-fidelity profile inpainting across three dimensions: maximizing numerical accuracy, capturing temporal fluctuation, and preserving spatial topological correlations.

key: t:research on virtualization based planning optimization method for distribution networks integrating multi source power signal feature
title: Research on virtualization-based planning optimization method for distribution networks integrating multi-source power signal feature
venue: International Conference on Computer Vision, Pattern Recognition and Detection
abstract: To enhance medium-to-long-term planning capabilities of distribution networks under uncertain conditions, this study constructs a virtualization optimization method driven by multi-source power signals. Based on feature extraction and temporal alignment of heterogeneous data, a feature fusion model utilizing mutual information weighting is established to generate a unified embedding representation. A virtual resource node set is constructed through resource attribute mapping (), integrating multidimensional metrics such as capacity, volatility, and reliability to form a dispatchable high-dimensional modeling system. Building upon this, a multi-objective optimization framework is introduced, designing an objective function encompassing system investment costs, power losses, uncertainty mitigation, and supply reliability, while establishing a feasible constraint domain. A hybrid optimization process combining NSGA-II and CVaR evaluation mechanisms is developed to achieve rapid convergence of the Pareto solution set and quality control of the solution space. Simulation analysis conducted on the IEEE 33-node system demonstrates that the proposed method exhibits significant advantages in system loss control, regulation cost optimization, and robustness enhancement, validating the effectiveness of multi-source feature fusion and virtualization strategies in distribution network planning scenarios.

key: t:probing multipole alignment in the beyondplanck ensemble using the power tensor formalism
title: Probing Multipole Alignment in the BeyondPlanck Ensemble using the Power Tensor Formalism
abstract: We present a comprehensive Bayesian test of statistical isotropy in CMB using end-toend posterior samples from the BeyondPlanck framework. Extending the power-tensor methodology, we replace single best-fit maps with full posterior ensembles, thereby propagating uncertainties from noise, gain fluctuations, and foreground separation directly into anisotropy diagnostics. We examine the quadrupole–octopole alignment, low-ℓ axial alignments, and high-ℓ power entropies, and we generalize the power-tensor formalism to E-mode polarization to provide the first probabilistic assessment of polarization isotropy from power-tensor statistics. While the BeyondPlanck maximum-a-posteriori solutions reproduce previously reported anomalies, in power-tensor alignment metrics, the marginalized posterior distributions of these statistics exhibit substantially broader credible regions. Within the power-tensor framework, this broadening reduces the apparent level of tension with ΛCDM once instrumental and astrophysical covariance is incorporated. A comparative study with Cosmoglobe and NPIPE demonstrates that several apparent anisotropic features correlate with specific systematic modes, particularly time-dependent gain variations. Our results suggest that high-significance anomalies found in traditional frequentist analyses may be overestimated due to incomplete treatment of correlated uncertainties, and that a Bayesian sample-based power-tensor analysis provides a more robust characterization of

key: t:cross modal semantic alignment method for heterogeneous power data based on association learning models
title: Cross-modal semantic alignment method for heterogeneous power data based on association learning models
venue: Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Data Processing
abstract: In power equipment monitoring scenarios, the limited extraction of vibration signals results in low semantic alignment accuracy. To address this, we propose a cross-modal semantic alignment method for heterogeneous power data based on an association learning model. For vibration signals and infrared thermal imaging data, we design hierarchical and multiscale association feature extraction processes respectively. By establishing semantic associations through typical correlation analysis, we resolve issues such as significant modal differences. A cross-modal alignment model is constructed, proposing a joint loss function based on contrastive learning. Robustness is enhanced by incorporating outlier detection algorithms to achieve deep data fusion. The model employs an improved association learning framework to optimize semantic consistency and introduces an evidence-theoretic decision fusion mechanism to quantify alignment reliability. This approach achieves highly robust semantic alignment across multi-source heterogeneous power data, providing cross-modal semantic support for tasks such as equipment condition assessment. Experimental results demonstrate that initial multimodal data exhibits scattered distribution in semantic space. After processing by the proposed method, data shows significant clustering effects, forming compact cluster-like distributions. In noise interference experiments, the mean absolute error remains below 0.8% without interference, with 95% sample erro

key: t:comparison on power cycling test consistency across technical routes core stress relative parameter alignment as the key to equivalence
title: Comparison on Power Cycling Test Consistency Across Technical Routes: Core Stress-Relative Parameter Alignment as the Key to Equivalence
venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement
abstract: Power cycling test (PCT) is one of the most significant tests to evaluate the long-term reliability of power semiconductor devices. The accuracy and consistency of PCT results are fundamental to the reliability assessment and lifetime prediction. However, the emergence of diverse technical routes from different manufacturers for PCT equipment on the market has raised critical concerns regarding measurement consistency and result comparability. This study presents a systematic investigation into the equivalence of distinct technical routes and test benches from three aspects of the tested power semiconductor devices: the steady-state operational parameters, the transient thermal behavior, and the PCT lifetime. It is revealed that equipment based on different technical approaches achieves consistent measurement of both steady-state parameters and transient thermal characteristics at the same conditions. Then, the lifetime should be consistent according to the lifetime models. Furthermore, closely aligned PCT lifetime distributions across different test benches are demonstrated, with Weibull mean lifetime differing by merely 3% under the identical core stress-relative parameters. The findings confirm that PCT results are governed by the core stress-relative parameters rather than by the specific test equipment or ancillary adjustment parameters. In practical applications, this work helps to develop a fundamental methodology that shifts the focus from equipment-specific validatio

key: t:data driven multi objective optimization of 10 0 4 kv distribution transformer placement in urban power networks
title: Data-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization of 10/0.4 kV Distribution Transformer Placement in Urban Power Networks
abstract: The global energy system is undergoing a significant transformation driven by rapid electrification, urbanization, and the emergence of new categories of electricity consumers. In particular, the increasing load density in low-voltage distribution networks within urban areas requires a reconsideration of conventional methodologies for the placement of transformer substations. Traditional planning approaches are often based on empirical service radii or static demand factors and therefore fail to adequately reflect the complexity of modern urban power systems. This study proposes a multi-objective optimization model for the optimal placement of transformer substations in 10/0.4 kV urban distribution networks. The proposed model simultaneously considers power losses, economic costs, and system reliability. In addition, the design load model is extended through the introduction of a comfort coefficient that captures additional electricity consumers typical of modern urban infrastructure, including HVAC systems, elevators, pumping systems, and electric vehicle charging stations. In contrast to traditional empirical approaches, the transformer service radius is modeled as a physical parameter determined by voltage drop limits, cable thermal constraints, and failure intensity. The optimization problem is solved using the Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II). Each candidate solution generated by the algorithm is validated through AC load-flow simulations performed in

key: t:lightweight power quality disturbance recognition for edge monitoring in distribution networks
title: Lightweight Power Quality Disturbance Recognition for Edge Monitoring in Distribution Networks
venue: 2026 5th International Conference on Green Energy and Power Systems (ICGEPS)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of distributed generation and power electronic loads, distribution networks exhibit stronger nonstationary behaviors and high-frequency disturbances, leading to growing power quality issues at feeder and transformer levels. For edge monitoring scenarios, disturbance recognition methods must achieve stable and realtime performance under limited computational resources. This paper proposes a power quality disturbance recognition approach based on time-frequency representation and a lightweight convolutional network. Short-time Fourier transform is employed to construct spectrograms that explicitly capture time-frequency structures of disturbances, followed by a lightweight convolutional network for classification. A noise-view constraint is introduced during training to enhance output stability under varying signal-to-noise ratios. Experimental results based on synthetic data demonstrate that the proposed representation effectively differentiates typical disturbance types, and stratified SNR evaluation quantitatively reveals the impact of noise on discriminative structures. The proposed framework provides a deployment-oriented solution for edge-level power quality monitoring in distribution networks.

key: t:data driven identification of active distribution network to customer transformer relationships a power active admittance regression method
title: Data-Driven Identification of Active Distribution Network-to-Customer Transformer Relationships: A Power Active Admittance Regression Method
abstract: Accurate identification of customer transformer relationships in distribution sub-zones is a fundamental prerequisite for the refined management of low-voltage distribution networks and the integration of distributed generation sources. Addressing current issues such as missing records, non-standard wiring and unclear boundaries between multiple sub-zones, this paper proposes an identification method based on the Power Admittance Regression Algorithm (PARA). Based on the fundamental laws of electrical circuits, this method constructs a regressible model of the linear relationship between the total admittance at the transformer end and the admittances at each consumer end. By utilising electrical data collected simultaneously from smart metres and distribution transformer terminals, it formulates the identification of consumer transformer relationships as a problem of minimising regression residuals. For three typical operating conditions—pure residential load, mixed residential and commercial load, and photovoltaic connection at the feeder terminus—constrained least-squares regression models and binary regression models incorporating PV variables were established respectively; ridge regression regularisation was introduced to suppress multicollinearity and enhance model robustness. Simulation tests were conducted using a dataset comprising 150 consecutive time sections and 70 test nodes (of which 60 were customers within the local substation area and 10 were interference node

key: t:power supply reliability optimization algorithm for user side resource coordination in distribution automation systems
title: Power Supply Reliability Optimization Algorithm for User-Side Resource Coordination in Distribution Automation Systems
venue: 2026 International Conference on Intelligent Engineering and Next-Gen Healthcare Systems (IEHNS)
abstract: With the widespread integration of user-side resources such as distributed power sources, energy storage systems, and adjustable loads into distribution networks, traditional power supply reliability assurance methods relying on network-side scheduling face new challenges. To address this issue, this paper proposes a collaborative power supply reliability optimization algorithm for user-side resources in distribution automation systems. First, a power supply reliability assessment model is constructed, including System Average Outage Time (SAIDI), System Average Outage Frequency (SAIFI), and Unsupplied Power (ENS). A collaborative operation model for distributed power sources, energy storage systems, and demand response resources is also established. Based on this, a multi-objective optimization algorithm is designed to achieve collaborative scheduling of multiple types of user-side resources. The results are validated through a typical distribution network simulation example. The results show that under the user-side resource collaborative optimization model, the system SAIDI decreases from 2.86 h/household/year to 1.78 h/household/year, the unsupplied power decreases from 38.52 MWh/year to 21.43 MWh/year, and the average recovery time is shortened from 96.3 min to 65.8 min. Meanwhile, under a load fluctuation scenario of ±15%, the node voltage deviation is only 0.029 pu, and the average computation time remains within 1.12 s. The research results show that the proposed coll

key: t:identification of line faults in power distribution networks supported by micro phasor measurement units
title: Identification of Line Faults in Power Distribution Networks Supported by Micro Phasor Measurement Units
venue: Journal of Advanced Engineering and Computation
abstract: Power distribution systems are becoming more complex and vulnerable day by day due to the increasing penetration of non-linear loads, renewable sources, and critical expansions of the overhead supply networks. Thus, the chances of distribution line failures have increased. On this occasion, effective fault detection aids in developing predictive maintenance strategies, helping utilities reduce downtime and utilize resources more effectively. In this paper, a machine learning (ML)-based methodology for fault detection on overhead distribution lines has been presented. The study has demonstrated the application of the two typical tree-based ML classifiers, i.e., random forest (RF) and extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost), to diagnose distribution line faults with the help of a micro phasor measurement unit (μPMU) supported data set. The study reveals a μPMU allocation strategy and data collection method to aid in the preparation of the data set. The classification models are structured to classify the location of the line faults, followed by the faults' type, based on the prepared data set for a test network. The efficiency of the RF and XGBoost has been verified through a quantitative comparison with the existing approaches.

key: t:cadnm a chain active distribution network with soft open points for optimal power schedule of expressway considering multi uncertainties
title: CADNM: A Chain Active Distribution Network With Soft Open Points for Optimal Power Schedule of Expressway Considering Multi-Uncertainties
venue: IEEE transactions on intelligent transportation systems (Print)
abstract: To address the challenges of limited resilience and high operational costs in current expressway power supply systems under extreme conditions, a chain active distributed network model featuring dynamic SOPs is introduced. This model leverages flexible interactions among network nodes to facilitate optimal power flow distribution and energy dispatch. An uncertain dataset, based on the Wasserstein distance, is constructed to account for the diverse characteristics of power sources and loads on expressways. Using this dataset, a “Traffic-Electrical” coupling model for typical power scenarios is developed to identify the optimal SOP installation locations under improved flow capturing location model constraints, thus forming an active network with SOPs. A two-stage optimization model targeting both the “robustness” and “economy” of the power supply system is designed with the support of a novel “NSGA-II-PSO” heuristic algorithm. Simulations of the “Taohuaping-Dingyuan” segment of the G30 “Lian-Huo Expressway” demonstrate the model’s effectiveness, with a 9.74% reduction in average voltage offset and a 3.78% decrease in dispatch costs compared to traditional networks, confirming its robustness, flexibility, and cost-effectiveness.

key: t:sspc based secondary power distribution system for typical aircraft application
title: SSPC – Based Secondary Power Distribution System for Typical Aircraft Application
venue: IOSR Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
abstract:
The increasing adoption of More-Electric Aircraft technology has created demand for efficient and
lightweight electrical power distribution systems. This work presents the design and simulation of a Solid-State
Power Controller (SSPC)-based system for a typical aircraft application. SSPCs provide several advantages
over conventional electromechanical circuit breakers, including improved reliability, reduced maintenance
requirements, and enhanced system protection. A ±270 V DC aircraft power distribution architecture is
considered, and the SSPC is implemented using Silicon Carbide MOSFETs. The complete secondary power
distribution system is modeled and simulated in LTspice to evaluate its performance under normal operating
and fault conditions. Wide-bandgap SiC MOSFETs address the limitations of conventional circuit breakers by
enabling microsecond-level fault isolation and programmable inverse-time I²t overcurrent protection. Two
topologies were designed and simulated: SSPC-S using a single CAS350M12BM3 SiC MOSFET module (4mΩ,
1200 V) and SSPC-M using five parallel C2M0025120D discrete devices at ±270 V DC with 85°C. LTspice
circuit simulations validated turn-off transient behaviour with and without MOV and capacitive snubber
protection and verified the protection profile of the I²t tripping curve. SSPC-S achieves a steady-state junction
temperature of 105°C and peaks at 146°C under the worst-case cascaded overcurrent scenario, both within the
175°C device limit. SSPC-S is co

key: t:optimization of multienergy farm distribution network dispatch considering on site consumption of photovoltaic power
title: Optimization of multienergy farm distribution network dispatch considering on-site consumption of photovoltaic power
venue: International Conference on Energy System, Electricity and Power
abstract: To enhance the grid's photovoltaic absorption capacity and reduce operational costs on large-scale farms, this study proposes an optimized dispatch method for multi-energy farm distribution grids that accounts for local photovoltaic consumption. First, refined mathematical models are constructed for irrigation, electric agricultural machinery, fertilizer processing, and greenhouse loads, alongside output models for distributed power sources like PV and biogas. Based on these, a source-load coordinated optimization dispatch model is established with dual objectives: minimizing operational costs and maximizing local PV consumption rates. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces daily operational costs during typical summer and winter days while increasing local PV consumption rates. Through load shifting and multi-energy coordinated output, the system effectively regulates loads during peak and off-peak electricity pricing periods, enhancing energy self-consumption levels while reducing electricity costs. This approach provides a reference for scheduling farm distribution grids with high renewable energy integration.

key: t:comparative assessment of contactors and sspcs on grid safety in 540 v dc aircraft power distribution systems
title: Comparative Assessment of Contactors and SSPCs on Grid Safety in 540 V DC Aircraft Power Distribution Systems
abstract: This paper presents a comparative assessment of mechanical contactors and solid-state power controllers (SSPCs) in 540 V DC aircraft power distribution systems. An arc-based mechanical contactor model and an SSPC model with typical protection functions are established and validated by experimental waveforms. The two devices are then compared under typical loads and fault conditions in terms of switching behavior, fault isolation, and grid impact. The results show that mechanical contactors are more prone to arcing, inrush current, overvoltage, and interruption delay, while SSPCs can mitigate transient disturbances through controlled switching, current limiting, and fast protection. Under short-circuit conditions, the contactor requires about 20-25 ms for fault interruption, whereas the SSPC interrupts within about $150 \mu ~\mathrm{s}$ with much smaller disturbances to the bus and adjacent branches. Overall, SSPCs show clear advantages over mechanical contactors for 540 V aircraft DC distribution branches with low-to-medium current levels.

key: t:mitigation techniques on the effect of power quality issue in distribution system
title: Mitigation Techniques on the Effect of Power Quality Issue in Distribution System
venue: IOP Conference Series: Earth and Environment
abstract: This research investigates the impact of various nonlinear loads on the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in distribution system. The primary objective is to analyse the extent of THD caused by these loads and to evaluate the effectiveness of filter-based mitigation techniques. A comprehensive modelling approach is undertaken using the IEEE 14-bus test system, incorporating typical nonlinear load profiles. Subsequently, several mitigation strategies including Shunt Passive Filter (SPF), Shunt Active Power Filter (SAPF), and Hybrid Filter are designed and implemented. The performance of these filters is assessed based on IEEE 519 standards, focusing on their ability to reduce harmonic distortion and improve overall power quality. The findings reveal that, although all filter types contribute to the reduction of THD level, the hybrid filter demonstrates the most effective performance by combining the stability of passive components with the adaptive control of active filtering.

key: t:a multi time scale source load matching driven assessment method for the reverse power flow limit of distributed pv in distribution networks
title: A Multi-Time-Scale Source - Load Matching-Driven Assessment Method for the Reverse Power Flow Limit of Distributed PV in Distribution Networks
venue: 2026 3rd International Symposium on New Energy Technologies and Power Systems (NETPS)
abstract: To address the issue that, after the integration of high-penetration distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems, reverse power flow risk in distribution networks is jointly affected by seasonal variations, intraday fluctuations, and short-term random disturbances, while existing assessment methods mostly rely on a single worst-case operating condition or typical scenarios at a single time scale and therefore cannot accurately characterize the impact of source - load temporal mismatch on reverse power flow boundaries, this paper proposes a dynamic assessment method for reverse power flow limits of distributed PV in distribution networks that considers multi-time-scale source - load matching characteristics. First, a source - load matching index system is constructed from three dimensions, namely seasonal/monthly energy balance, daily/hourly power coupling, and 15-minute shortterm fluctuations, while feeder partition characteristics and electrical distance are introduced to characterize the spatial matching relationship between sources and loads. Second, based on source - load correlated scenario generation and typical scenario reduction, a reverse power flow limit assessment model is established that takes into account the peak value, duration, and over-limit probability of reverse power flow, with comprehensive consideration of constraints such as node voltage, line thermal stability, reverse power transfer capability of distribution transformers, and operating modes. Finally, a h

key: t:adaptive fusion suppression method of fault current and voltage using power converter for arc suppression in active distribution networks
title: Adaptive Fusion Suppression Method of Fault Current and Voltage Using Power Converter for Arc Suppression in Active Distribution Networks
abstract: Single phase-to-ground faults in distribution active networks can cause serious hazards, such as fire accidents, electrical shocks, and power outages. Power converters can be connected to a neutral point of distribution networks to suppress fault current and voltage until the fault arc disappears. However, typical current- or voltage-based arc suppression methods alone, using the controls of proportional-integral, proportional-lagging, backstepping, or sliding mode, etc., cannot adapt to uncertain and variable fault resistances, causing a long transient response process and residual fault current and voltage, resulting in the fault arc not being extinguished quickly and reliably. This article proposes a nonlinear adaptive controller design-based fault current and voltage fusion suppression method. The proposed method integrates both fault current and voltage suppression methods, and covers variable and unknown fault resistances. It can follow Lyapunov's asymptotic stability. Thus, the proposed method can better suppress fault current and voltage, and adapt to variable fault resistances. Simulation study and experimental validation demonstrate that not only are the fault current and voltage simultaneously suppressed without a long transient response time under different fault resistances, but also the residual fault current and voltage are smaller, compared with the typical methods.

key: t:optimization of active power losses for high voltage distribution grids using mixed integer quadratic programming
title: Optimization of Active Power Losses for High-Voltage Distribution Grids Using Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming
abstract: The energy transition is leading to increased loading of high-voltage distribution grids (HVDGs), which in turn results in higher active power losses. In addition, the meshed network structure typical for German 110 kV grids enables transit power flows originating from the superimposed transmission grid (TG). These transit power flows may further increase grid loading and active power losses. This paper presents a sensitivity-based mixed-integer quadratic programming (MIQP) approach for active power loss minimization in meshed HVDGs. The proposed methodology achieves near-real-time computation times while maintaining high accuracy by means of a piecewise linearized alternating current (AC) formulation. In addition, losses of static synchronous compensators (STATCOMs) and transformer-reactance variations are explicitly modeled. Reactive power provision by distributed energy resources (DERs) and STATCOMs, as well as discrete tap positions of power transformers (PTs) and phase-shifting transformers (PSTs), are considered as control variables. The proposed approach is validated using hourly snapshots of a real German HVDG provided by a distribution system operator (DSO). The results demonstrate a significant reduction in active power losses together with computation times suitable for near-real-time applications.

key: t:application of multi scale deep learning model for power quality disturbance identification in distribution networks
title: Application of Multi-Scale Deep Learning Model for Power Quality Disturbance Identification in Distribution Networks
venue: 2026 8th International Conference on Information Science, Electrical and Automation Engineering (ISEAE)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of distributed energy resources and nonlinear loads into distribution networks, power quality disturbance problems have become increasingly severe, and traditional identification methods based on handcrafted feature extraction face bottlenecks of declining accuracy and insufficient generalization in complex scenarios where multiple disturbance types coexist. This paper proposes a Multi-Scale Deep Learning Model (MSDLM) that integrates a multi-scale convolutional feature extraction module, a bidirectional long short-term memory network, and a channel attention mechanism, enabling simultaneous capture of local transient features and global temporal dependencies of power quality disturbance signals. On a dataset generated through IEEE standard-based simulation containing seven typical power quality disturbances and their composite disturbances, the proposed model achieves an overall recognition accuracy of 98.670%, representing improvements of 3.420% and 7.150% over conventional convolutional neural networks and support vector machines respectively, while demonstrating superior robustness under varying signal-to-noise ratio conditions.

key: t:model based multi agent reinforcement learning for power supply assurance in distribution network
title: Model-Based Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Power Supply Assurance in Distribution Network
venue: 2026 IEEE 3rd International Conference on Electrical Power Systems and Intelligent Control (EPSIC)
abstract: Distribution networks host critical loads and mission-critical activities, where even brief power interruptions can result in significant economic losses and safety impacts. This paper proposes a model-based multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) framework for power supply assurance in a distribution network. The problem is formulated as a cooperative Markov decision process in which heterogeneous agents coordinate grid import, photovoltaic(PV) generation, battery energy storage system(BESS), diesel generators, and flexible loads under network and operation constraints. A high-fidelity simulation environment is constructed as a digital model of the system, and a centralized training and decentralized execution(CTDE) paradigm is adopted. Case studies on a typical summer day show that supply–demand balance is well maintained, the BESS mitigates evening peaks, the diesel unit provides short emergency support, and node voltages remain close to 1.0 p.u., demonstrating its potential for application in the distribution network.

key: t:a new approach to filtering static attenuator based on unequal power distribution network
title: A New Approach to Filtering Static Attenuator Based on Unequal Power Distribution Network
venue: IEEE Microwave and Wireless Technology Letters
abstract: In this letter, a new method to design fixed attenuator with bandpass filtering response is proposed originating from the unequal power distribution network (UPDN). Specifically, by keeping one of the output ports being matched, a two-port attenuator can be naturally formed. In addition, the attenuation is dependent on the different power division ratios between two output ports. As a typical illustration, the square patch resonator is analyzed and adopted to accomplish the desired unequal magnitude outputs. Furthermore, the bandpass filtering response is achieved through double stack-coupled patch resonators. For the sake of accurate fixed attenuation and good port matching, two grounded chip resistors are attached to the square patches. Finally, a practical filtering attenuator with fixed 20-dB attenuation is fabricated and measured. Results from the simulation and measurement are in good agreement with each other, well validating the concept.

key: t:urban power distribution system morphological characteristics analysis and reconfiguration strategy
title: Urban Power Distribution System Morphological Characteristics Analysis and Reconfiguration Strategy
venue: 2026 6th Power System and Green Energy Conference (PSGEC)
abstract: In response to increasingly complex grid structures and the growing demand for highly reliable power supply in urban power systems, this paper investigates the morphological characteristics of urban distribution networks in China and proposes multi-scenario operational strategies for supply assurance. The structural evolution of typical Chinese urban distribution networks is first summarized to identify key requirements for reconfiguration-oriented operation. To address practical operational requirements, a multi-scenario supply assurance strategy is proposed, and a reconfiguration optimization model is formulated by jointly considering network-loss cost and voltage deviation. A case study based on real urban distribution network in China are conducted to validate the proposed method. The results show that the proposed approach can effectively balance economy and security under different scenarios, demonstrating its applicability to reconfiguration-oriented operation in urban distribution networks.

key: t:preliminary analysis of components cost distribution for a low enthalpy geothermal power plant
title: Preliminary analysis of components cost distribution for a low enthalpy geothermal power plant
abstract: In the present work, a focused analysis of the cost-components distribution of a low-enthalpy Rankine cycle using supercritical carbon dioxide (sCO2) as the working fluid is made. This investigation aims to evaluate the cost distribution of the main sCO2 components and identify the most cost-intensive elements to support future techno-economic assessments of low-enthalpy power plants. More specifically, the present work explores the utilization of a low-enthalpy geothermal field located in the Sidirokastro area, in Serres region in Greece, for approximately 250 kW of power generation, with a maximum geothermal water source temperature of 78 °C. To estimate the thermodynamic performance of this specific geothermal field, a thermodynamic model was developed, modelling a transcritical Rankine cycle using sCO2 as the working fluid. The thermodynamic model was developed using the Cape Open to Cape Open (COCO) simulator and incorporated the most recent available data describing the geothermal source properties and typical performance characteristics of the main thermodynamic cycle components. Furthermore, the Peng-Robinson equation of state was used, to estimate the thermophysical properties of sCO2. For the calculation of the low-enthalpy power plant, a preliminary assessment of the purchase cost of the main components of the geothermal power plant was performed, based on the most updated correlations from international literature.
